definition: Aesthetic value is the pleasing or displeasing quality assigned to something as beautiful, sublime, or ugly. In the associationist view described here, that value comes wholly or partly from earlier pleasures or displeasures that the object, or something related to it, brings back to mind rather than from the object’s form alone.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Association (in aesthetics); pinned source text

reasons: The packet defines aesthetic value in terms of how pleasure in the presence of the beautiful or sublime is explained by association, but it does not explicitly state a general definition of “aesthetic value” as a “pleasing or displeasing quality assigned to something” (nor does it explicitly cover “ugly” as part of that definitional phrasing).
Because the first sentence’s characterization of the term is not directly supported by the supplied packet, the definition as a whole is not fully defensible against the packet.
